anomalies.observed: On the Ethernet page the two RJ45 indicator LEDs are cross-connected with respect to their net names: ETH_LEDY is run through R2 (470R) to D24, which is valued LED_GREEN, while ETH_LEDG is run through R3 (470R) to D23, which is valued LED_YELLOW. Both cathodes/anodes return to LED_3.3V_POWER_SW.
anomalies.expected: A net named for a colour (ETH_LEDY = yellow, ETH_LEDG = green) should drive the LED of that colour, as everywhere else on the board where the LED value field states the colour (D4/D12/D17/D28/D29 etc.).

evidence.quote: ETH_LEDY - R2 470R - D24 LED_GREEN - LED_3.3V_POWER_SW ; ETH_LEDG - R3 470R - D23 LED_YELLOW - LED_3.3V_POWER_SW (Ethernet page, J25/RJ45 area)

anomalies.impact: The Ethernet link/activity LED colours are interchanged relative to the intended indication, so the green and yellow status lamps report the wrong Ethernet state to the operator.

anomalies.observed: The CAN transmit/receive activity LEDs D12 (LED_GREEN) and D17 (LED_YELLOW) are driven from the 3.3 V buffer outputs U18/U19 through series resistors drawn as 5R6 (5.6 ohm), while every other indicator LED on this board (D4, D23/D24, D28/D29, D30) uses 130R-1k.
anomalies.expected: A current-limiting resistor in the same family as the board's other indicator LEDs (roughly 130R-560R) for a green/yellow LED fed from 3.3 V; 5.6 ohm would allow well over 200 mA.

evidence.quote: U18 - R15 5R6 - D12 LED_GREEN ; U19 - 5R6 - D17 LED_YELLOW (LEDs page)

anomalies.impact: When CAN traffic toggles TXLED/RXLED the LEDs and the driver outputs would be grossly over-driven (LED and gate destruction), i.e. the CAN activity indicators would fail instead of indicating.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is indicated: on the Ethernet page the colour-coded LED nets are crossed (ETH_LEDY drives the green LED D24 and ETH_LEDG the yellow LED D23), and the CAN activity LEDs D12/D17 are fed through 5R6 series resistors that are two orders of magnitude too small for a 3.3 V indicator LED. Confidence is limited because both findings rest on text read from the supplied drawing.
